_meta.indication: Indicated to reduce the incidence of catheter-related bloodstream infections (CRBSI) in adult patients with kidney failure receiving chronic hemodialysis (HD) through a central venous catheter (CVC); indicated for a limited and specific population

pivotal_trials.design: Single, multicenter, double-blind, randomized, active-controlled Phase 3 trial comparing Defencath catheter lock solution to the active control heparin (1,000 USP units/mL)
pivotal_trials.population: Adult subjects (≥18 years) with kidney failure (ESRD) undergoing chronic hemodialysis with a permanent, tunneled silicone or polyurethane catheter
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint: time to CRBSI (revised during trial to incidence of CAC-adjudicated CRBSIs)
pivotal_trials.result: Final analysis: 9 CAC-adjudicated CRBSIs (Defencath) vs 32 (heparin), 71% risk reduction (95% CI 38%, 86%), p=0.0006; hazard ratio 0.29 (95% CI 0.14, 0.62)

key_safety: Most frequent adverse reactions (≥2%): hemodialysis catheter malfunction (17% vs 12% heparin), hemorrhage/bleeding (7% vs 9%), nausea (7% vs 11%), vomiting (6% vs 8%), dizziness (6% vs 4%), and thrombocytopenia (2% vs 1%). Loss of catheter patency occurred more frequently in the Defencath arm (63 subjects, 16%) vs heparin (48 subjects, 12%). Serious adverse reactions in 40% (Defencath) vs 42% (heparin).
target_moa: Combination of taurolidine, a thiadiazinane antimicrobial (a derivative of aminosulfonamide-taurinamide) that transfers methylol groups interacting with bacterial and fungal cell walls, and heparin, an anticoagulant; taurolidine reacts with cell wall constituents of gram-negative bacteria and neutralizes endotoxin activity
modality: Small molecule (taurolidine) combined with heparin, formulated as a catheter lock solution

advisory_committee.vote: An advisory committee meeting was originally scheduled for January 14, 2021 but was cancelled; the review team concluded there were no issues that would benefit from Advisory Committee discussion.

summary.text: Defencath was approved under the Limited Population Pathway for Antibacterial and Antifungal Drugs (LPAD) pursuant to section 506(h) of the FDCA, following a Priority review. The drug had received Fast Track and Qualified Infectious Disease Product (QIDP) designations. A deferred pediatric study is required as a postmarketing requirement.
